newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs lifted by weak machinery data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs lifted by weak machinery data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were firm but off their highs in late Tuesday trade after being lifted by news of weak machinery orders data and the Nikkei's failure to sustain its gains.
Japan's Economic Planning Agency said private machinery orders were likely to rise 4.5 percent in the April-June quarter after falling 7.0 percent in the first quarter.
The forecast was on the lower end of market expectations of between plus five and 10 percent.
Signs Japan's economic recovery was not gathering ground would put a damper on recent speculation a rate hike was in the offing, dealers said.
"The Nikkei had some effect. When it was being sold down, Euroyen and JGBs pushed higher," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended 14.40 points lower at 20,129.11 after rising as high as 20,452.35.
The lead December Euroyen contract stood at 98.93 at 1204 GMT after hitting a high of 98.96 against an IMM close at 98.87.
June JGBs settled at 124.12 against their previous 123.29.
"I think the market is a bit short so people were just covering. But I would sell December Euroyen anywhere above 99.00," the trader said.

Eurodollar futures finished mostly flat in lacklustre trade ahead of a slew of U.S. economic indicators this week, including April retail sales, wholesale prices, consumer prices and industrial production.
December Eurodollars finished at 93.730 against their IMM close at 93.735 on scant volume of 6015 lots.
